detail.content:
# Ⅰ. Overview ## 1.1 Overview This policy governs access and use of the TikTok Shop Partner Center Platform ("TTSPC"), and applies to any user of the TTSPC platform ("Partner"), including with respect to the marketing, advertising and offering of any services and/or products on the TTSPC. * Create a positive service subscription environment on the TikTok Shop Service Market ; * Provide a reliable subscription experience to merchants who subscribe to the service. All partners selling services through the TikTok Shop Service Market must operate under our guidelines. ## 1.2 Scope The Violation Management Regulations for TikTok E-Commerce Partners covers the service release requirements for partners with respect to the marketing, advertising and offering of any services and/or products on the TTSPC. **IMPORTANT: Partners ensure that** **TikTok Shop Partner Center** **listings,** **TikTok Shop** **Service Market sales and services provided comply with applicable laws and regulations.** Our guidelines are intended to facilitate compliance by partners. They are not exhaustive and are not intended to serve as legal advice. If partners have questions about the laws and regulations of their products, we encourage partners to seek independent legal advice. Our guidelines are regularly updated. It is the service partner's responsibility to check this page regularly to ensure they are adhering to our current guidelines. ## II. Definitions * Partners means any company, person, user, individual or other entity that sells services and services on the TikTok Shop Service Market . * The capitalized terms contained in this policy shall have the meaning set forth in our TikTok Shop Partner Center Terms of Service. ## III. Management of Violation Points * The TikTok Shop adopts a violation point-based management mechanism for partners' violations. After TikTok Shop determines that a partner has violated the rules (in its absolute discretion), the corresponding points will be issued based on the severity of the violation. TikTok Shop reserves the right to take corrective action for any violation of the TikTok Shop Partner Center Terms of Use, including but not limited to removal of a partner and its services. When the points of a partner reach a certain level, determined in TikTok's sole discretion, TikTok is guaranteed to take corrective action against the partner.This is without prejudice to any other rights and remedies that may be available to TikTok Shop for your violation of these rules, or any other TikTok Shop terms or policies." * The initial violation points of a partner is 0 point and the upper limit is 120 points, which are cleared on the 180th day (30 June at 23:59:59 GMT+8) and the last day (31 December at 23:59:59 GMT+8) of each calendar year. * Enforcement measures for different levels of violation points are shown below: | | | | --- | --- | |
**Accumulated Violation Points** |
**Measures: no operational support** | |
30 points |
30 days | |
40 points |
60 days | |
60 points |
90 days | |
90 points |
180 days | |
120 points |
No longer allowed to enter the Service Market | |
Remarks |
1. If the accumulated points are more than 90, the partner must provide a description of the situation and a rectification report within the service suspension period after receiving the point notice. If the information is not provided or the information is unqualified, the platform has the right to continue deactivating all the services for the partner.


2. Partners who are issued 120 points for a single violation will be removed and added to the blacklist, and their violation points will not be cleared. The platform reserves the right to "blacklist" partners and publicize them on the Service Market. | * Based on the severity of violations, we may take action in addition to the necessary corrective actions. These measures include suspending and/or terminating your access and use of the TTSPC, including the advertising, marketing and/or offering of any of your services and/or products on the TikTok Shop (in each case, in whole or part). A non-exhaustive list of additional actions we may take is included below: 1. **Limit Available Services** , which means partners are not allowed to sign up for any ad resources or other recommended activities, but this does not affect their presence on TikTok. 2. **Partner termination,** which means the partner is removed from the Service Market, and all services under the partner's name are deactivated. All TikTok API calls of its services (if any) are stopped; the terminated partner is permanently prohibited from re-entering the Service Market. 3. **Actions for other accounts of the partner,** TikTok Shop has the right to impose the same actions on other accounts of the partner based on the severity of the violation. 4. **Freeze and deduct commissions and fees** derived from policy violations or frauds conducted by the partner or by others in its network (such as sellers or creators). ## IV. Partner Violations and Corrective Actions ### 1. The information provided is not compliant #### 1.1 Falsification of information **[Violation behaviors]** The onboarding and business documents provided by the partner involve falsified information, which is found during moderation (including but not limited to onboarding moderation and review) or reported by others. These violation behaviors include but are not limited to: * Providing fraudulent company registration certificates. * Providing fraudulent company information. * Failing to provide true and valid identity information of merchants/partners/creators. * Failing to sign true and valid contracts with creators/merchants/enterprises. * Submitting other fraudulent documents required to be reviewed during onboarding. * Fraudulent test results, including but not limited to communicating with merchants for product exchange, disclosing test items in advance, issuing qualified reports without testing and making promises about test results **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points are issued for each violation. #### 1.2 Incomplete information **[Violation behaviors]** The onboarding documents provided by a partner do not meet the requirements of TikTok Shop, which is found during moderation (including but not limited to onboarding moderation and review) or reported by others. These violation behaviors include but are not limited to: * Failing to provide complete company registration certificates. * Failing to provide complete information of business size. * Failing to provide trademark/patent certificates or other qualification documents required by TikTok Shop from time to time. * Failing to provide identity information of merchants/partners/creators required by TikTok Shop from time to time. **[Enforcement]:** * 30 points are issued for each violation. #### 1.3 Not meeting the entry criteria **[Violation behaviors]** The qualification of a partner does not meet the platform onboarding standards, which is found during moderation (including but not limited to onboarding moderation and review) or reported by others. These violation behaviors include but are not limited to: * Failing to provide additional documents required by the platform to substantiate compliance with onboarding standards after they are updated. * Repeated onboarding: the same entity onboarded more than once of the same service provider type. * Having been terminated by other platforms. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points are issued for each violation. #### 1.4 Not updating the business information in a timely manner **[Violation behaviors]** During its application for entry into TTSPC and its operation in TikTok Shop Service Market, a partner fails to update the platform on any changes of its business information within 30 days after the changes. These violation behaviors include but are not limited to: * Failing to update company registration certificates in the case of any changes. * Failing to update business address in the case of any changes. **[Enforcement]:** 30 points are issued for each violation. ### 2. Improper, Harmful, Illegal or Malicious Acts #### 2.1 Improper transfer of benefits **[Violation behaviors] Any improper, harmful, illegal or malicious acts, including but not limited to:** including but not limited to: * A partner pays bribes to employees of ByteDance (including partner shareholders, directors, supervisors, senior managers and the active staff) or commit acts in violation of the Code of Conduct of ByteDance Business Partners. * The existing interests between agencies and merchants have not been reported, and their services have been facilitated. * A partners uses bribery, fraud and other illegal means to obtain operational resources and business opportunities. A partners uses bribery and other means of benefit transfer to improperly obtain operational resources and business opportunities. * Use of the TTSPC to cause harm to any third party. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points are issued for each violation. #### 2.2 Tax violations **[Violation behaviors]** Acts that violate, or may violate, any applicable tax laws and regulations or lead to damage to users or TTSPC, including but not limited to: * A partner refuses to provide or fails to duly provide valid invoices or receipts to TTSPC users (i.e. the payer). * A partner commits or is suspected of committing tax evasion, tax fraud, invoice fraud, or other tax violations during their use of TTSPC. **[Enforcement]:** * For minor circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * For general circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * For serious circumstances, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 2.3 Undue profits **[Violation behaviors]** Acquiring benefits fraudulently, which is detrimental to users or the platform. Examples are: fraudulent activity and misleading merchants/creators, acquiring platform incentives by dishonest means, abnormal invitation of tender, treating merchants differently to gain profits and forcing them to buy services. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * For serious circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * For particularly serious circumstances, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 2.4 Conducting authorisation business in violation of rules **[Violation behaviors]** A partner conducts authorised business in violation of rules. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Claiming to be a partner/brand partner/regional partner/partner a certain type without or beyond the scope of authority (For example, an MCN/CAP partner pretends to be a TSP partner). * Production of fake licences and promoting or profiting from them. * After withdrawing from being a certain type of partner, still using its name or previous cases to continue recruiting merchants or operating services. * An agent or a partner fraudulently use official names, fake licensing or other means to collect fees, build cooperation, recruit merchants, etc. * Production of fake/fraudulent licences/documentation/unofficial issuance of licences, and using them for promotion, such as publicity and campaigns or other monetisation. * Unauthorized transfer or use of licences. * After withdrawing from being a partner, still using its partner licence to engage in activities, publicity and distribution, etc. * A partner carries out activities such as product promotion in the name of the platform or regarding the platform without or beyond the scope of authority. **[Enforcement]:** * For serious circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * For particularly serious circumstances, 120 points will be issued for each violation. ### 3. False advertising #### 3.1 False advertising / exaggerated promises **[Violation behaviors]** A partner transmits content which contains false information, misdescribes facts, exaggerates, or overpromises, or commits other acts which can cause misunderstanding; or a partner conducts or assists in false advertising or other deceptive and misleading behaviors that violate the advertising laws, including but not limited to: * Display of unapplied shop/creator accounts as success stories, fraudulent use of success stories in communication with merchants/creators and promises that cannot be fulfilled; giving description that contains false qualifications and false capabilities/services (e.g. failing to provide short video filming services as advertised), services are falsely claimed to be free of charge, and other situations that violate relevant laws and regulations such as advertising laws (including but not limited to service and detail description which contains absolute terms) * Giving false advertising and exaggerated promises in the process of merchant recruitment or operation. * False promises about granting certain permissions, etc. * False promises about traffic support, etc. * The service functions described in the service title, detail page, internal pop-up banner, publicity banner and other spaces are inconsistent with the actual service provided, or the information is false or exaggerated. * Giving false advertising and exaggerated description, or abusing promises or overpromising about the functionality. * Advertising on behalf of merchants who have not subscribed to the service. * Making false promises about category service capabilities that the partner does not actually have. * A partner makes exaggerated promises of the results. * Giving false advertising and exaggerated promises of the service results, causing complaints of merchants. * Conducting or assisting in false advertising or other deceptive and misleading behaviors that violate the advertising laws. * Using absolute terms when advertising service products. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 20 points will be issued for each violation. * For serious circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. ### 4 . Suspected fraud #### 4.1 False/fraudulent transactions **[Violation behaviors]** False/fraudulent transactions, including but not limited to: * Earning incentive fees through false transaction behaviors abusing campaign incentives, partner incentives, etc. * A partner helps merchants with false transactions, publicly charges fees for the help and promotes the help. * A partner hires companies to use false transactions to improve its experience scores . * False transactions maliciously made by competitors; e.g. malicious order brushing of viral products of competitors. * False transactions of creators or celebrities; e.g. false transactions of fans and brokerage companies. * False transactions of the Service Market orders. * A partner conducts improper profit-making services, such as follower boosting and order brushing. * Using order brushing to drive the scores in the Service Market. * TikTok has sole discretion in determining false/fraudulent transactions. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * For serious circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * For particularly serious circumstances, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 4.2 Fraud **[Violation behaviors]** Based on the comprehensive judgement of TikTok, there are reasons to believe that a partner has no intention to perform the contract and is suspected of illegally obtaining other people's property and infringing on other people's property rights for the purpose of gaining illegal profits. **[Enforcement]:** 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 4.3 Significantly not as described (SNAD) **[Violation behaviors]** The services displayed in the showcase or LIVE are completely different from the actual services received by merchants. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * For serious circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * For particularly serious circumstances, 120 points will be issued for each violation. ### 5. Platform information security #### 5.1 Information leakage **[Violation behaviors]** All partners leak information(sharing confidential information, commercially sensitive information, personal data etc.) of the platform or other parties, including but not limited to: * Including but not limited to the leakage of data to third parties without the authorization of the platform, the leakage of business data to other entities without the authorization of the merchants and the leakage of users' personal information without the authorization of the platform users, causing the risk of leakage of confidential matters. * Leakage of key business information(GMV data etc.), sharing key business information in public without the authorization of the platform, including but not limited to accepting interviews with the media, consulting companies, other third parties, etc. * A partner collects, displays, discloses, uses or authorizes others to use the service operation data without authorization. Such service operation data include but are not limited to personal data such as user name, mobile phone number, address, transaction data, interface data and other service usage data. * A partner mistakenly transmits a full report which contains test items and standards that must not be transmitted to external parties, resulting in the leakage of project standards. * A partner leaks information of product test items, warehouse and factory inspection standards and passing standards which are unpublicized to merchants to influence them to place orders. * A partner is reported by an external party and verified to have conducted data leakage behaviors. * A partner illegally uses third-party softwares with Trojans implantation, resulting in the leakage of business/consumer information. * A current or former employee of a partner is reported to have misused or leaked merchant/consumer information. * Privately developing batch decryption tools for merchants without the permission of or reporting to the platform, resulting in consumer information leakage . * TikTok has sole discretion in determining false/fraudulent transactions. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 5.2 Data security **[Violation behaviors]** All partners commit acts which undermine platform data security, including but not limited to: * A partner collects TikTok Shop or the Service Market account numbers, passwords, or other ID credentials of merchants. * A partner collects data beyond the authorization of merchants and the Service Market or takes any technical measures to obtain data from TikTok Shop and the Service Market/the open platform without express authorization. * A partner saves, displays, aggregates (data of multiple merchants and stores, for example), leaks, uses or authorizes others to use the service operation data without authorization. Such service operation data include but are not limited to personal data such as user name, mobile phone number, address, industry data, transaction data, interface data and other service usage data. * A partner's application includes obtaining and analyzing data of the platform, merchants or consumers and has caused negative impacts on the platform, merchants or consumers. * A partner improperly discloses the user data it obtains to any third party. * A partner's application includes the function of obtaining and analyzing information and industry intelligence such as business data or consumer personal data. * A partner fails to rectify under the relevant requirements of TikTok Shop such as security capabilities, security risks and timely security response. * The platform detects sensitive API calls, but the partner fails to truthfully report the sensitive information requests—a case of subjective omission and concealment of API logs. * Subjectively concealing and clandestinely developing batch export function of plain text information. * Clandestinely storing private data of the platform's merchants and consumers in plain text in violation of the platform rules. * A partner clandestinely use technical means to call the platform's decryption APIs through regular polling without authorization to illegally obtain private data of consumers of the platform. * TikTok has sole discretion in determining false/fraudulent transactions. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 5.3 Application security violations (including improper APIs) **[Violation behaviors]** All partners commit acts that violate the platform application security, including but not limited to: * Collecting data by obtaining merchants' login status with the TikTok Shop account and password login function embedded in the application. * The partner leaks sensitive information such as high-risk ports, management APIs or source code directories of the application system to external parties. * Behaviors that actively endanger system security, such as account privilege escalation and backdoor program installation, appear in the partner's application. * The partner's application interferes or attempts to interfere with the proper functioning of the open platform, other partners' applications or any part or functionality thereof. * The partner's application system has security bugs that can cause data leakage and are not fixed in time (such as direct or indirect support for plug-ins and crawling for order information/chat history). * The partner's application is not upgraded or modified based on the relevant security requirements of the platform. The submitted information for review is untrue and incomplete (including but not limited to failing to complete security-related upgrades of the application under the platform announcement). Failing to disclose the whole set of shared data of a single application such as its web application, servers and databases to the platform when applying for security access. * Failing to complete safety-related upgrades or risk rectification within the specified time limit under the platform's safety-related regulations. * The partner fails to rectify under the relevant requirements of TikTok Shop platform notification such as security capabilities, security risks and timely security response. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 5.4 Malicious use of the platform loopholes **[Violation behaviors]** All partners maliciously exploit the platform loopholes it found and conceals them deliberately. **[Enforcement]:** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. ### 6. Disrupting the platform #### 6.1 Posting prohibited and sensitive information **【Violation behaviors】** Partners threaten the security of the platform and put TikTok Shop at risk. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Political risk: Involving politically sensitive, ethnic, military, diplomatic, or historical figures. * Sensitive topics: Discriminatory, offensive remarks concerning race, colour, religion, etc. * Partners use the words "TikTok Shop" in any way that infringes on the rights of third parties or violates the law. **【Enforcement】** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.2 Unfair competition **【Violation behaviors】** Partners act in violation of competition law or disrupt the service market by acting in an unfair or malicious manner. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners disparage others and spread false information about them to damage their rights and interests. * Partners deceive, induce or force merchants to use its service only but do not provide services afterwards. Partners do not end the partnership even after being reported/complained about. * Partners form a partnership with creators/merchants without consent and do not end it even after the creators/merchants have provided evidence of the unauthorised binding. * partners attempt to negatively impact other partners, such as plagiarism. * To attract merchants to place orders in the service market, partners lower the testing standards to increase the test pass rate. * Other practices of unfair competition. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.3 Promotion in the name of TikTok **【Violation behaviors】** Partners use the name/logo of TikTok.These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners promote themselves in the name of TikTok or use the name/logo/template/signal. * Partners promote themselves in the name of an invalid official event/product. * Partners pretend TikTok ( including use the name/logo/template/signal ) or their staff pretend to work at TikTok, when they recruit creators or cooperate with merchants. * Partners use the name and logo of the platform and its affiliates. * Partners use official or suggestively official expressions or logos on the primary image, title, or product detail page of the service description. * TikTok has sole discretion in determining false/fraudulent transactions. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.4 Circumvent platform management **【Violation behaviors】** Partners have the intention to circumvent or have already circumvented the platform managements(Platform rules and Operations). These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners or their staff do not fulfil their regulatory requirements and assist or allow the merchants to circumvent platform managements. * Partners introduce or cooperate with unauthorized quality assessment agencies and provide services for them without the authorization and permission of the platform. * Other behaviors aiming to circumvent platform management. **【Enforcement】** * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.5 Harrassment **【Violation behaviors】** Partners use uncivil language to harass, defame, denigrate or abuse users/platform staff. Or, partners use irritating words or phrases to abuse others or harm their legitimate rights and interests. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners harass brands or merchants who have already onboarded TikTok e-commerce by requesting to establish a service marketplace partnership . * Partners harass, insult, threaten, and intimidate merchants or creators or give them unfounded negative reviews for retaliation. * Partners interrupt others' every day lives, causing physical or mental harm or bad influence . * Partners send a large number of spam messages (e.g. unknown verification codes) to others by phone, SMS, email, etc., and contact others frequently. * Partners repeatedly contact others late at night or in the early morning hours, causing inconvenience to others. * Partners insult or threaten others through phone calls, SMS, emails or comments or send repugnant items to others. * Partners abuse platform staff verbally or in writing. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.6 Manage accounts improperly **【Violation behaviors】** Partners manage accounts improperly. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners apply, transfer, lend, rent or disclose application and service accounts to any third parties without the platform's permission. * Partners steal others' accounts or infringe on others' rights to physical safety and to property. * Partners have their accounts stolen due to improper management, causing adverse impact on platform users. * Partners apply, lend, sell or transfer application and service accounts on behalf of others without the permission of the platform or the owner of the account being handled by the Partner. **【Enforcement】** * 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.7 Induce merchants to violate the rules **【Violation behaviors】** Partners induce/abet merchants or creators to break the rules. These behaviors include but are not limited to: * Partners assist or guide merchants to violate platform rules. **【Enforcement】** * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.8 Improper use of the rights of others 【 **Violation behaviors** 】The service information published by partners or the service provided by the partners improperly uses other people's trademark rights, copyrights, patents and other rights. It includes but is not limited to the following scenarios: * Use success stories of other partners for publicity. * The names, nicknames, avatars, logos, slogans, products, etc. used by the partner are acts of impersonating the identity of others and infringing on the legal rights of others. * The content provided by partners involves plagiarism or other acts that infringe on other people's intellectual property rights or other legal rights. **【Enforement】：** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 6.9 Other behaviors that disrupt the platform **【Violation behaviors】** Other behaviors that disrupt the platform or are detrimental to the interests of merchants and creators. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. ### 7. Misplacement of categories #### 7.1 Misplacement of categories **【Violation behaviors】** Behaviors where the listed service category is inconsistent with the actual category, including but not limited to the following scenarios: * The category relevant to the service type is not selected when listing, or the category does not match the one chosen during onboarding. * The core function of the application (meaning: the function required by the category when it is first listed) must meet the category definition in the access rules of the category. After the first review and launch of the application, the partner changed the function of the application, resulting in the core function obviously not conforming to the definition of the category. **【Enforcement】** 30 points will be issued for each violation. ### 8. Prohibited & restricted service #### 8.1 Prohibited Service **【Violation behaviors】** The behavior of partners publishing prohibited functions or services through the platform. Including but not limited to the following scenarios: * Information suspected of infringing on legal rights or interests (including but not limited to intellectual property rights, the same below) held by third parties. * Link or include goods or services without authorization. * Other goods or services prohibited by laws and regulations. **【Enforcement】：** * For general circumstances, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 8.2 Unsupported Service **【Violation behaviors】** Partners publish functions and services that are not supported by the platform for sale through the platform, including but not limited to the following scenarios: * Application functions or partners damage the rights and interests of users, or provide convenience or assistance for others to damage the rights and interests of users. Examples include software that can steal pictures/videos from other stores; recording the livestream from other stores and using it for your own store. * Features that disturb users or affect users' browsing path. * Image storage services, or services that extract image links on product detail pages and replace them. * The partner conducts illegal profit-making services, such as order brushing, buying followers, etc. * There are links to other websites in the front-end module, or the store page automatically jumps to somewhere else without any operation. The front-end module does not provide the function for merchants to directly delete or uninstall the code. * The application contains relevant links or instructions that inform or induce users to log in, register and use other platforms other than TikTok Shop cooperated platforms. * Direct users off TikTok Shop and its cooperative platforms to complete ordering and transactions, or provide services with such potential risks, i.e. transaction security risks or user data leakage. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. ### 9. Service product information is not compliant #### 9.1 Service product information is not complete **【Violation behaviors】** The published services or functions are not related to the platform business; the service content lacks necessary information, or includes non-compliant behaviors. Including but not limited to the following scenarios: * The service information contains marketing information unrelated to the TikTok Shop business. * Service functions are not related to TikTok Shop. * The service name or service details description repeats and piles up key words. * The detailed description is incomplete, and the corresponding introduction module is missing, which affects the user experience. * The service name, details page, service or service partner's logo contains offensive words. **【Enforcement】：** * For general circumstances, 10 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 20 points will be issued for each violation. #### 9.2 Inconsistent service product information **【Violation behaviors】** The key information of the service is inconsistently described, including but not limited to: service cycle, service content, price, after-sales service, etc. **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 10 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 20 points will be issued for each violation. #### 9.3 Other language **【Violation behaviors】The act of publishing service product information in the non-official language of the local country** **【Enforcement】** * For general circumstances, 10 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 20 points will be issued for each violation. ### 10. Non-compliance in operation #### 10.1 Failure to deliver services as agreed **【Violation behaviors】** The partner fails to provide the promised service to the merchant under the agreement made between the partner and the merchant, impairs the rights and interests of the merchant, or enters a dispute with the merchant/creator due to unfair or improper terms, and the disputes caused cannot be resolved, resulting in negative influence. It includes but is not limited to the following scenarios: * After the merchant/creator and the partner sign or reach a cooperation agreement, the partner fails to fully perform the services in the agreement, or the service quality does not meet the agreed standards, or the merchant/creator cannot contact the partner, or the partner terminates service for no reason (the agreement does not allow termination for convenience). * After terminating the cooperation agreement according to the conditions stipulated in the agreement signed by the merchant/creator and the partner, the partner refuses to perform the post-termination obligations, such as: refunding the merchant/creator, returning the store to the merchant/creator (including but not limited to returning account operation access) . * After the merchant/creator and the partner reach a cooperation agreement, the partner fails to provide services under the promised service content ( promise includes: paper contracts, email correspondence). * The service partner has not completed cooperation agreement, or written commitment, including: permissions (such as store backend operation permissions, data viewing permissions, etc.) have not been returned to the merchant/creator, and data (such as merchant/creator data during the cooperation period) has not been returned to the merchant/creator. * Failure to integrate key capabilities of the open platform within the specified time as required by TikTok Shop. * Due to service fulfillment problems, the merchant was punished by TikTok Shop or samples got lost, etc. * For testing items with a fixed testing time limit, the feedback times out, resulting in the delay of the merchant's onboarding process. **【Enforcement】：** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 10.2 Service abnormality **【Violation behaviors】** Abnormal service provided by the partner, including but not limited to the following scenarios: * The application service is unstable, continuously inaccessible. * The application service the application service is defective. The application service is unavailable for a long time, or a batch of merchants are affected. * The partner cannot provide services normally due to attacks such as DDOS. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 10.3 Software or Service Discontinuation **[Violation behaviors]** The software or services provided by partners stop for non-platform reasons. This type of violation behaviors include but are not limited to: * Service was temporarily interrupted due to a system upgrade, computer room adjustments, line switching, etc. Partners interrupt the service without prior notice to the user on the service page three days in advance. * Partners close the software/suspend the service in advance without the consent of the merchant. * Partners have stopped their services, or we judge that they are not actually providing services. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 10.4 Negative after-sale **[Violation behaviors]** Partners reject, do not respond, respond over time, or do not handle service improvement suggestions without viable reasons when dealing with the after-sales requests of merchants and creators. These behaviors, deemed by the platform at TikTok's sole discretion as the partners' fault, include but are not limited to the following scenarios: * Partners don't provide after-sales service: No or non-compliant after-sales services. * It is found that the partners' contact information is invalid or their phones are shut down. Or response timeout three times/reject phone call/do not provide after-sales services. * Failure to deal with merchant complaints promptly for more than five days, or failure to respond to feedback from merchants and platforms for more than two days. * Users complain about partners, and the platform becomes aware: more than three times per month. * Partners do not correct their behaviors one month after receiving the warning of violations. * Partners refuse to provide services for merchants and give no feedback after receiving warnings. * Partners are involved in a refund dispute. The circumstances are severe, and partners do not respond to the issue promptly. * Partners fail to handle customer complaints properly, resulting in an escalation of public rhetoric and spillover effects. **[Enforcement]:** * For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. * If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. #### 10.5 Failure to meet platform operation requirements **[Violation behaviors]** Partners fail to meet the operational capability requirements of the platform, providing poor service or being unable to fulfil the duties of the contract. This type of violation also refers to cases where partners and their affiliates severely violate rules in other business modules of ByteDance or are penalized by judicial authorities. Including but not limited to: * Partners do not meet the platform's [operational metric requirements](https://partner.tiktokshop.com/doc/page/647050289fe1f7028441a6e9). * Partners do not attend necessary training as required by the platform. * Partners do not meet or are considerably lower than expectations. * The person in charge can not be contacted for 30 days, and there are significant problems or stagnation in partners' internal cooperation and operation. * Partners violate contracts and do not go LIVE or perform poorly. * Products are of poor quality. * Partners fail to update and submit the latest qualifications as required by the platform. * Partners do not fulfil the cooperation agreement signed with the merchants/creators or get involved in disputes with creators and cause a negative impact for being unfair, containing unfair requirements in contracts, or failing to resolve issues promptly. * Partners do not manage signed creators properly as required by policies including but not limited to TikTok Shop Creator Performance Evaluation Guidelines, and TikTok Shop Content Guidelines. * Partners promise to participate in marketing events but withdraw without permission. * Partners provide poor services in areas such as properties, training, business consulting, quality inspection and logistics, and market-oriented services. * Partners do not manage their agents properly (e.g. Agents infringe upon other's rights or violate laws and regulations). * Partners provide invalid contact information, respond passively, and do not provide relevant materials as required in the case of an administrative investigation or legal proceedings. **[Enforcement]:** For general circumstances, 30 points will be issued for each violation. If the circumstances are serious, 60 points will be issued for each violation. If the circumstances are particularly serious, 120 points will be issued for each violation. ## Appeal 1. If partners believe that an enforcement action has been taken against them in error, they may file an appeal within seven days of receiving the violation notice from email([tts.partner.warning@tiktok.com](mailto:tts.partner.warning@tiktok.com)). Otherwise, it will be deemed that the partners approve the enforcement. The platform will review the appeal and tell the partners the results of receiving the appeal. 2. An appeal raised by partners does not affect the validity, execution and publicity of the decision already made by the platform. Only when an appeal is successful will we remove any corrective actions issued. 3. Partners can refer to the violation notice to choose the correct appeal channel. (email:[tts.partner.appeal@tiktok.com](mailto:tts.partner.appeal@tiktok.com)). 1）The subject of the email must include the following: Partner ID + Order ID + [Appeal] 2）The content of the email must include the following: ① Partner ID, Order ID (text); ② Violation ID + Violation reason; ③ Appeal reason and relevant materials, including but not limited to chat records, screenshots, links, photos, recordings, etc. ## Appendix 1. These rules will become effective on December 10, 2022. 2. The platform will sample the services provided by partners from time to time. If the partners and their services violate the rules, the platform will take enforcement actions accordingly. Meanwhile, the platform will suspend all online operational and promotional resources and give a public warning. Only when partners have corrected all the violation behaviors and the period of corrective actions ends can they resume regular operation. 3. The platform manages and takes enforcement actions against all accounts and services of partners. If the same identity authentication information is used or the actual controller of multiple accounts is determined to be the same person after investigation, they are all regarded as the same partner. If partners and their services violate the rules, the platform reserves the right to take enforcement actions of the same severity on all the accounts and services of the same partner. 4. The determination and handling of violations shall be based on the evidence of violations or the facts determined by the platform (the platform has the right to adjust the enforcement actions in light of the actual situation). 5. If more than one violation is found, the platform will penalize the more severe violation. It does not mean that the partner has only one violation. 6. If the partner violates the rules again or repeatedly, the platform may take multiple enforcement actions based on the rules the partner has violated and the number of violations. 7. Partners must abide by national laws, administrative regulations, departmental rules and other normative documents. These rules apply to any suspected violations covered. TikTok reserves the right to deal with violations not included at its discretion. However, TikTok's enforcement actions on partners do not exempt them from legal liabilities. Partners must always abide by TikTok's guidelines and their affiliates' agreements.

detail.title: 【TikTok Shop - Cross-border Partner】 Onboarding Guide for SEA
detail.content:
## Ⅰ. Overview The rules in this guide apply to cross-border partners(TikTok Shop Partners) with **their company entity (or branches) registered in Mainland China and Hong Kong** (companies based in Taiwan and Macau are not supported for the time being. Contact your operation manager for further information, if needed.) that work with creators, sellers, brands on TikTok Shop. TikTok Shop Partner types include, but are not limited to, TSP, MCN, affiliate partners (TAP), and others. This document, as well as the onboarding rules, **will be updated periodically as the platform's business continues to develop. Please revisit these onboarding rules regularly** to ensure that your business is in compliance with the latest rules. # Ⅱ. Applicable Categories and Scope of Service [Applicable Categories and Scope of Service for different operating markets and roles of partners](https://bytedance.sg.larkoffice.com/sync/GLC4dEjYPsbaHzbXXZ9lQaJMg6d) > Note: The category of **"Operations Coaching" (training, mentoring)** is marked gray, as the qualifications for partners are relatively high. At present, **the number of TikTok partners onboarded to this category is 0. Sellers are advised to take full consideration before cooperating with partners of this category.** # Ⅲ. Partner On-boarding Qualifications Depending on the **type applied for, TikTok Shop requires partners to meet the following** qualifications: | **Partner Types** | **Market** | **Professional and Operational Capabilities** | **Specific** **Requirements** | **Company Qualifications** | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **MCN** | SEA | **Creator service capabilities:**

* Possess creator resources with real management contracts
* Competent in creator content production/marketing
* Ability to properly select or bundle e-commerce products
* A roster of solid e-commerce live hosts and a professional live operations team

**Content operations/e-commerce service capabilities:**

* Experienced with practical e-commerce livestream skills (live broadcast setup, consistent production of livestream content).
* Equipped with the ability to create e-commerce short videos
* A roster of solid e-commerce live hosts and a professional live operations team


**Bonus items**
**Tools**

* Self-developed tools that are able to reach and connect with sellers and creators in bulk, including but not limited to, data tools, product selection platforms for creators, and other tools, etc.

**Advertising abilities**

* Familiar with TikTok's advertising tools (promote, live shopping ads, etc.)
* Data analysis capabilities (LIVE data review, account growth diagnostics, ROI calculation abilities, etc.) | **Location requirements** :

* ≥ 1 high quality livestream studio, and dedicated office space.

**Contract proof:**

* Able to reference **≥ 3** [TikTok accounts operating in the SEA country with at least 1,000 followers]

**Staffing:**

* A dedicated TikTok operations team (including content production, livestream operations personnel) with a team size ≥ 10 people. | * The enterprise has been registered for more than 1 year
* The enterprise is not operating abnormally
* Other requirements

> Mainland China: the business license scope includes the services required for this category
> Hong Kong, China: qualifications and verifications for corporate entities in various regions.
| | **TikTok** **Affiliate Partner (TAP)** | SEA | **Creator connection/operation capabilities:**

* Ability to consistently and efficiently develop business with creators, and form collaborations with a large number of local creators in the target market
* Ability to track creator performance and promote creators to post e-commerce content


**Seller acquisition/product selection capabilities:**

* Equipped with abundant seller acquisition resources (with brands, industrial zones, government, etc.)
* Ability to plan promotions and campaigns
* Ability to properly select and bundle e-commerce products


**Bonus items**
**Tools**

* Self-developed tools that are able to reach and connect with sellers and creators in bulk, including but not limited to data tools, product selection platforms for creators, and other tools, etc.

**Advertising abilities**

* Familiar with TikTok's advertising tools (promote, live shopping ads, etc.)
* Data analysis capabilities (LIVE data review, account growth diagnostics, ROI calculation abilities, etc.) | **Location requirements:**

* A physical office space in either China or the SEA countries

**Contract proof:**

* Cooperating with ≥ 10 SEA creators

**Staffing:**

* A dedicated TikTok operations team with a team size of ≥ 3 people.
| | | **TSP** | SEA | **Account incubation capabilities**

* Abundant resources of e-commerce content creators
* Capable of incubating/operating/marketing creator accounts
* Ability to properly select and bundle e-commerce products

**Content operation capabilities**

* A roster of solid e-commerce live hosts and a professional live operations team
* Experienced with practical e-commerce livestream skills (live broadcast setup, consistent production of livestream content).
* Equipped with the ability to create e-commerce short videos


**Bonus items**
**Tools**

* Self-developed tools that are able to reach and connect with sellers and creators in bulk, including but not limited to data tools, product selection platforms for creators, and other tools, etc.

**Advertising capabilities**

* Familiar with TikTok's advertising tools (promote, live shopping ads, etc.)
* Data analysis capabilities (LIVE data review, account growth diagnostics, ROI calculation abilities, etc.) | **Location requirements :**

* A dedicated office space
* ≥ 3 high-quality and physical livestream studios

**Staffing:**

* A dedicated TikTok Shop team of 10 or more people, including 2 full-time foreign live hosts or at least 4 non-foreign live hosts fluent in English

**Livestream planning:**

* Average ≥ 3 sessions/week of effective e-commerce livestreams

> *Definition of effective e-commerce livestreams:*

> * *1. The livestream must be an e-commerce live stream (includes a shopping cart) with products already uploaded to TikTok Shop.*
> * *2.The duration of livestream is longer than 1.5 hours, with more than 6 products featured in* *the* *livestream*
> * *3. The livestream displays, introduces, and promotes products for sale, while also guiding viewers to place orders*
| | | | SEA - acquisition partners | **Equipped with abundant seller acquisition resources** (with brands, e-commerce sellers, industrial zones, e-commerce partners, etc.)
Familiar with TikTok Shop SEA's on-boarding rules (on-boarding conditions, seller acquisition categories, etc.) | **Location and Staffing Requirements** :

* A dedicated office space with a team size of ≥ 10 people

**Contract proof:**

* **≥ 3** [successful cases of TikTok Shop cross-border seller acquisition events with ≥ 50 sellers in attendance per event (providing seller acquisition event posters, event locations, information of registered sellers, photos) ]
* Fill in a detailed introduction of the company's capabilities, organizational structure, successful cases, competitive advantages, etc., and upload the company's PDF or PPT materials for records
* **≥ 100 sellers** successfully acquired and onboarded (with the deposit payment rate is ≥ 70%) | * The enterprise has been registered for more than 1 year
* The enterprise is not operating abnormally
* Other requirements

> Mainland China: the business license scope includes the services required for this category
> Hong Kong, China: qualifications and verifications for corporate entities in various regions.


* The enterprise registered capital of 500,000 + | # Ⅳ. Required Materials As part of the application process, cross-border partners must submit relevant business qualifications, as well as any other additional information and documents that may be required. Upon receiving the application, TikTok Shop will review the materials, and may require supplemental information and documents for a second round of review before approving applicants as **onboarded TikTok Shop partners**. Any personal data will be treated in accordance with TikTok's privacy statement. ## A. General Information | **Partner Type** | **Market** | **Professional and Operational Capabilities** | **Company Qualifications** | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | Introductory Powerpoint | Business License | Legal Representative Identification | Contact Information | |
**General**
Required for all applications for any type of partner in all markets
| |
**Company introduction powerpoint**
The presentation should introduce the company's business in detail, and include authentic visuals for illustration purposes. The partner's company introduction (should include):

1. Areas of business and seller acquisition strategy
2. The company's organizational structure
3. Success cases
4. Business plans & outlook
5. Link to an uncut video of the company | Scanned copy or photo of the **original 3-in-1 or 2-in-1 business licence**
1) Ensure that the company is not on the the list of businesses of abnormal operations, and that services provided are within the scope of the business license issued.
2) The expiration date of the license should be at least more than 15 days in the future.
3) Licenses and documents must be clear, complete, and valid.
4) The company name on the business license/registration documents must match the name of the company being onboarded.
Note: Hong Kong entities should submit both the Corporation Registration Certificate (CR) and the Business Registration Certificate (BR) at the same time. | Scanned copy or photo of the **front and back** of the original ID card of the company's legal representative.
1) The legal representative's ID card
2) Must be a second-generation ID card
3) The ID needs to be clear, complete, and valid.
4) Legal representatives who are not residents of Mainland China can use passports or permanent residency cards issued by the People's Republic of China or issued by Hong Kong SAR. If a passport is used, a translated copy of the personal information page stamped with the official seal of the translation agency must be submitted concurrently. | **Company contact information,** including but not limited to

* Address
* Email
* Telephone number

> 1) Real and active
> 2) The registered person is the same entity/person as the applicant

detail.title: 【TikTok Shop Cross-border Partner】 Onboarding - Common Reasons of Rejection
detail.content:
This document is intended solely for TikTok Shop's cross-border partners as a self-assessment guide to identify and address common issues that may lead to the rejection of onboarding applications.
# Business License and ID
**1.1 Insufficient Information**
> Including but not limited to:

> * Partial or incomplete images (e.g., not the entire document is shown);
> * Documents with creased corners, causing information to be obscured;
> * Blurry or low-resolution images;
> * Missing back side of the legal representative’s ID card;
> * Non-original or altered documents.

**1.2 Expired Qualification**
Including but not limited to:
An expired ID card or one that is nearing expiration;
An expired business license or one that is nearing expiration.
*Note: Qualifications are considered "nearing expiration" if their validity is less than 30 days.*
**1.3 Qualifications Held for Less Than One Year**
The submission date in the partner system is less than one year from the establishment date on the business license.
**1.4 Unrelated Business Qualifications**
Including but not limited to:
The company's business qualifications are not related to the applied category (e-commerce operations).
**1.5 Inconsistent Entity Information**
Including but not limited to:
A mismatch between the company name on the business license and the name provided in the application (please include the original Chinese name and provide a Chinese translation if necessary);
Discrepancies in the legal representative's information compared to the business license.
**1.6 Repeated Onboarding**
Including but not limited to:
Using the same business license, mobile phone number, or email address across multiple applications;
Overlapping information with high-risk associated partners who have previously been, or are currently pending, removal from the platform.
**1.7 Operational Risks**
Including but not limited to:
The business license number is in the process of being canceled, or the legal representative status is flagged as abnormal.
**1.8 Unverifiable Business License Number**
Including but not limited to:
The business license number cannot be verified due to input errors, such as incorrect entries or confusion between similar characters (e.g., "0" and "O"; "1" and "I").
# Operational Experience
**2.1 Screenshots Not Taken Directly from the Account Dashboard**
Including but not limited to:
Photos taken of the screen with another device, rather than a direct screenshot (from either PC or mobile);
Screenshots that do not meet category-specific requirements;
Screenshots displaying the account's public view instead of the account management dashboard.
**2.2 Missing Account Information**
Including but not limited to:
Incomplete screenshots;
Screenshots without visible login account details;
Missing or incomplete account information.
**2.3 Non-Compliance with Platform Operational Standards**
Including but not limited to:
Inappropriate content in LIVE sessions.
# Company Introduction
**3.1 Incomplete Office Environment Display**
Including but not limited to:
Missing photos of the main entrance or reception area (e.g., no company logo visible);
Mismatched entity information (e.g., the office logo does not match the company name or logo on the application);
Non-original images (e.g., photos with watermarks from other platforms).
> **Requirements**
> **Three photos:**

> * Reception area with company logo
> * General office area
> * Live-streaming or meeting rooms

> **One video:**

> * A single, continuous, unedited video shot from a straightforward angle, clearly showing the surroundings.
> * The video must include the company logo on the main entrance, office area, live-streaming rooms, and meeting rooms.

**3.2 Office Environment Does Not Match the Company's Described Size**
Including but not limited to:
Office capacity does not align with the company's description (e.g., the number of workspaces or employees does not match the company's introduction).
**3.3 Missing Company Operations Description**
Including but not limited to:
No description of the company's main business activities.
**3.4 Missing Company Showcases**
Including but not limited to:
No showcase materials provided, or submitted examples are not related to the company.
**3.5 Logo Inconsistency with Application Company**
Including but not limited to:
For example, the logo says "ABC Company," but the application is for "XAS Company."
**3.6 Account Used for External Promotion**
Including but not limited to:
Account names containing email addresses, phone numbers, company addresses, or other contact information.
**3.7 Inconsistent Entity Information**
The company name displayed at the front desk or storefront does not match the information provided in the application.

> * If the storefront name is in Chinese, it must match the company name on the business license.
> * If the storefront name is in English, the information in the "partner_name" field must either overlap with or be identical to the storefront name.
> * If the storefront name is bilingual, the Chinese name should match the company name on the business license, while the English name must overlap with or be identical to the "partner_name" field in the application.

**3.8 Company Size Does Not Meet Onboarding Requirements**
Including but not limited to:
Office capacity or number of live-streaming rooms does not meet onboarding requirements;
Photos are taken outside working hours, showing no staff present.
**3.9 Low-Quality Live-streaming Rooms**
Including but not limited to:
Live-streaming rooms are poorly equipped or not actively in use.
# Impersonation of Official TikTok Shop or Other TikTok Affiliated Entities
**4.1 Office Decor Featuring TikTok Shop or Affiliated Logos**
Including but not limited to:
Displaying TikTok Shop or affiliated company logos or text in areas such as the company's reception, signage, or glass door stickers.
**4.2 Materials Featuring TikTok Shop or Affiliated Logos**
Including but not limited to:
Use of homophonic company names (including account names) or materials that resemble official TikTok logos or text;
Inclusion of TikTok logos or text in company introduction slides or promotional materials.

detail.title: US TikTok Shop Affiliate Partner (TAP)
detail.content:
# Overview This guide covers how agencies can use Partner Campaigns to create campaigns between Sellers and Creators. With this tool, Sellers can register and submit products to an agency's campaign, and determine the commission they would like to offer to the agency. Then the agency chooses the commission they would like to set for the managed or unmanaged Creators they've selected for the campaign. Agencies share product links with the Creators so they can add the products to their showcases and promote them. The commission splitting is then completed online via the tool. Partner Campaigns offers several benefits: * For Agencies: A new revenue stream that allows agencies to collect commission from Sellers by setting up affiliate campaigns on their behalf. * For Sellers: A way to outsource the creation of campaigns and selection of Creators to agencies. Sellers can apply to campaigns in the Partner Campaigns tab, described in more detail in the Seller experience section of this article. * For Creators: More opportunities to earn affiliate commissions from product lists curated by the agencies. Participating Creators do not have to be managed by the agency. # Onboarding Requirements Step 1: If you already have a TikTok Shop Partner Center account, skip to step 2. If this is your first time signing up for TikTok Shop Partner Center, press **Skip** in the Business Guide Page. Then, select **Content Management** as your Business category.
Step 2: If you already have a TikTok Shop Partner Center account, then navigate to **My account** and press **+ Category & market**.
Step 3: Select **Business category** and then press **View more**. Then select **Content Management (for TSP)** and then select **Content Management**.
Step 4: In TTSPC, navigate to the **Finance** section, and then to **Payment accounts**, where you will be prompted to submit your US W-9 tax information. This can also be accessed via the **Tax information** tab.
Step 5: Complete the W-9 information, providing all the necessary information, such as name, contact information, EIN, and supporting documentation. At the bottom of the page, you can preview the completed W-9.
Step 6: Once your Tax information is completed, return to the **Payment accounts** page and click on **Link bank account**. If you are unable to link your account at this time and the account status is listed as "under review," please try again in 24 hours.
# Setting up Campaigns Step 1: Enter the **Partner Campaigns** page in TTSPC. If you are unable to click on **Create Campaign**, return to the top of this document and ensure that you have completed the steps in the Onboarding Requirements section. Otherwise, click Create Campaign to get started. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/5f826276a4974ebeafcffb73465c83eb~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/503f05bf980646e0b84e504dfd7acd3a~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 2: Enter the relevant campaign information, such as the **Target market, Basic information, Seller information**, the **Commission rate requirement**, and your **Contact information**. * In the **Basic information** section, describe in detail what this campaign is about and make it compelling for Sellers to want to participate. * Set the **registration period**, which defines the dates during which sellers can register products to the campaign. * Set the **campaign period**, which defines the dates during which creators can promote the products. (**Note**: The start date for the registration period and the campaign period must be the same.) * In the **Seller information** section, you can choose to make the campaign open to all Sellers or restrict it to selected Sellers by entering their Shop Codes. * You can add up to 100 Shop Codes. * Sellers can find Shop Codes in the Seller Center by going to My Account-> Seller Profile-> Seller Information. * After you have filled in all the relevant details, click **Submit**.
Step 3: After clicking **Submit**, you will be taken to the main **Campaigns** page. All of your created campaigns will be listed here. To publish the campaign to Sellers, you ++must++ turn on the **Publish Toggle**. On this page, you can also create more campaigns by clicking **Create Campaign**. # Approving/Rejecting Seller Products Step 1: After Sellers have registered products for your campaign, you can click into the **Campaign details** page to see all the registered products, as well as the commission rates they are offering for this campaign. Note that this is the total commission rate that will be paid to you and the Creators in the campaign.
Step 2: On the **Pending** tab, you must choose to **Approve** or **Reject** a Seller's product registration. Note that after you approve the registration, you will not be able to modify the commission rates set by the Seller. If you reject the registration, you will be asked if you would like to allow the Seller to re-register, and you will be able to give the Seller a reason for the initial rejection.
![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/a49f1d0fe17540aa9ca3b7a39ea0334b~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/f2d7b5f3a01a4918b501b97cef9f01e2~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 3: You can navigate to the **Approved** tab (1) to see a list of approved products. Here, select products individually or in bulk (2), and then click on **Export links** (3) to generate links to share with the Creators, which will allow them to view the products in the campaign and add them to their showcase. In order to export the links, you must first set a **commission rate** (4) that you want to offer the Creators. It must be less than or equal to the campaign's total commission rate. For example, if the Seller is offering a campaign total commission rate of 30%, then the commission rate you offer to the participating Creators must be less than or equal to 30%. If you set the commission rate here as 15%, then that means Creators will receive 15% and you will receive the other 15% of the commission.
Step 4: Rather than sending individual product links, you can also create a list of products to send to Creators by clicking on **Product lists**.
Step 5: First, give your product list a name, then select the products you want to include in the list (up to 100), and then click **Next**. Then, set the commission for each product separately, or in bulk by selecting multiple products and then clicking **Setup commission in bulk**. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/6d81791716084f1dae367582925951da~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/f06444acf5be430bb26be48f85e2881d~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 6: After you've created a product list, you can view all the product lists in the **Campaign details** page. From here, copy the link to the campaign list, which you can then share with Creators. You can also edit or delete any existing lists. Note that you can only have up to 1000 lists, and each list can contain up to 100 products. If you reach the list limit, you must delete an existing list to add another one.
Step 7: When you choose to edit a list, you can **Remove** existing products, **Add more products**, or **change the commission rates** for existing products.
Step 8: Any Seller registrations you have rejected will appear in the **Rejected** tab. Here you can see whether or not you allowed the Seller to re-register the product.
Step 9: In the **Pending closed** tab you can see the Seller registrations that are about to close. Here you can **Approve** or **Reject** these registrations, as well as view the data and Creators for this registration. In the **Closed** tab, you can see the product registrations and the associated data for the ones that have already closed. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/1ddf2ad20c364a52827214073cebb3d7~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/76a20de16eef4ac191097c6e896d2352~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) # Creator & Seller Experience ## Seller Experience Step 1: Sellers can access agency campaigns by clicking on the **Partner Campaign** tab. From here, they can see all of the campaigns that are published in the **Campaign marketplace**. Sellers can (1) filter these campaigns by **All campaigns** or **Target campaigns** (i.e. campaigns that they were specifically invited to), (2) **Search** for specific campaigns or partners, (3) **Register** for a campaign, and (4) view their existing **My campaigns.**
Step 2: In the **My campaigns** tab, Sellers can click into a campaign to view more details, data, and re-register to a campaign.
Step 3: After clicking into a specific campaign, a Seller can view more details about the campaign and the agency organizing it. Here, the Seller can also register their products by clicking **Register products** and then adding them. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/d776a702a7074030ae44b6fd2fe2b4ac~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/5689d63f0d3b480bb5c3cc3651068de4~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 4: Once a Seller has registered a product, it will be listed as pending on the campaign until the agency has approved it.
Step 5: After a product has been approved by the agency, it will appear in the Ongoing tab. Here, the Seller can choose to cancel a specific product collaboration by clicking **Close**. The agency must then approve the cancellation request before it takes effect.
Step 6: In the **Rejected** tab, a Seller can view all the collaborations that have not been approved by the agency. There are two possible scenarios here. In the first scenario (1), the agency has rejected the registration, but has provided a reason why and has given the Seller the opportunity to **Re-register**. In the second scenario (2), the agency has rejected the Seller's product registration and blocked the Seller from registering the product again.
Step 7: In the **Closed** tab, Sellers can **View Data** for product campaigns that have already closed.
Step 8: In the **Performance** tab, Sellers can view the data for this specific campaign, including the registered products, the number of orders, and the commission totals. From here, Sellers can also **Export** the existing orders. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/9cea430da4bc43bab85c80d941cc0a73~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/54458e290eb9428db881235cb9e9de79~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ## Creator Experience Step 1: Once the agency provides a link to the Creator, the Creator can paste that link by going to TikTok Shop, and clicking on **Add product**, then the **link icon** on the top right of the page, and pasting the link into **Product URL**. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/1cf0f9448817458886307419bd0ee77c~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/054a88f1f6954455a82b35c1072e4008~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/e0ed7cf3e8c04752a8bf22ee41e89fd0~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 2: Once the Creator has entered the product link, the Creator will be prompted to **Add to showcase** and **Agree to the terms** and conditions of participating in the affiliate campaign.
Step 3: If the Creator receives a list link, then they will be shown a list of products in the campaign after accepting the terms and conditions. The Creator can **Add all to showcase** or add them individually. When a Creator clicks into a product details page, they can see the commission rate and **Add to showcase**. The commission rate that is shown to the Creator is the commission rate they are paid by the agency, not the Seller. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/3744b19d86cf4bbda128890224054175~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/afd6d46d1e2545ef92be7126f36a326d~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/098e6ace4da14b21b10dde962b92ce37~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/672f5aa0c234400d96573aeb0fadf6e1~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 4: In cases when the commission rate in this campaign is lower than the commission rate the Creator is already receiving for a product or list, the Creator will receive alerts that their commission will decrease if they add the products from this campaign. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/05dd7ab8f6ef459c9d2cc183d83d6778~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/e5a113ff21e84ec4a30924a00e8c10c8~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 5: If after entering a link, a Creator receives a **No available products yet** or **The product list wasn't found** message, it means that the campaign does not have any products in it yet or that the agency has deleted the product or list. ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/07f07ae2d1a248418f3d93e041344ebc~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) ![Image](https://p16-arcosite-sg.ibyteimg.com/tos-alisg-i-k9wyc2ijk0-sg/5f28494044684755880ec8ef0d0ba8cc~tplv-k9wyc2ijk0-image.image) Step 6: In the **Affiliate orders** page, Creators will be shown when a sale and commission is from an agency-led campaign.
# FAQ 1. What happens if the agency that created the Partner Campaign is also linked to one of the Creators participating in the campaign? The agency can only collect commission from the Seller. The agency cannot collect commission from the Creator, as this would be considered "double dipping." 2. What happens if the agency that created the Partner Campaign invites a Creator to the campaign who is managed by another agency? The agency that created the campaign will still receive a commission from the Seller and can decide how much of that commission to give to the Creator. The remaining commission that goes to the Creator is then split between the Creator and the agency that manages the Creator, based on the existing agreement between both parties. 3. Can sellers see creator-specific performance data? No, sellers cannot see creator-specific performance data. Sellers are only able to view product-specific performance data. Partner Campaigns are therefore recommended for sellers who are eager to outsource their work to agencies, but do not require detailed insights into creator-specific sales performance.
